title: Type 2 Diabetes: New Diagnosis and Initial Treatment

teaching.scope: Adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: confirm the diagnosis, agree an individual HbA1c target, choose initial treatment (including the triggers for insulin) and start safely. Checked against SDCPG 2021 (pp. 20, 28, 31, 35, 42, 46–48) and NICE NG28 (updated 18 Feb 2026, sections 1.2, 1.5, 1.8 and 1.13–1.22).
pitfalls: Starting an SGLT-2 inhibitor in a person on a ketogenic diet or with a recent DKA episode.
Delaying insulin in a person with catabolic features.
Applying one HbA1c target to every adult regardless of frailty or hypoglycaemia risk.
keyPoints: HbA1c above 10%, glucose above 300 mg/dL or catabolic features: insulin first.
Check DKA risk before an SGLT-2 inhibitor and warn about ketogenic diets.
Add drugs one at a time and recheck HbA1c every 3–6 months.

learningObjectives: Confirm type 2 diabetes with the Saudi diagnostic criteria and set an individual HbA1c target.
Choose initial treatment by comorbidity and recognise who needs insulin at presentation.

redFlags: HbA1c above 10% or glucose consistently above 300 mg/dL (16.7 mmol/L): start insulin or a GLP-1 receptor agonist (SDCPG pp. 47–48).
Weight loss, ketosis or hypertriglyceridaemia with severe hyperglycaemia: insulin preferred (SDCPG p. 47).
Previous DKA, intercurrent illness, dehydration risk or a very-low-carbohydrate or ketogenic diet: check before any SGLT-2 inhibitor (NG28 1.21.1).
Ketosis with vomiting or drowsiness is an emergency: use the Diabetic Ketoacidosis topic, not outpatient titration.
symptoms: Polyuria and polydipsia suggest glucose toxicity and need early insulin (SDCPG p. 47).
Weight loss with catabolic features (SDCPG p. 47).
Often found by screening of at-risk adults rather than by symptoms (SDCPG p. 20).
precipitants: Overweight or obesity, including abdominal obesity (SDCPG pp. 19–20).
Family history, previous gestational diabetes, PCOS, hypertension, dyslipidaemia or physical inactivity (SDCPG pp. 19–20).
Diabetogenic drugs: glucocorticoids, atypical antipsychotics, statins, antiretroviral therapy, anti-rejection drugs (SDCPG p. 20).
physicalSigns: BMI and weight at every visit (SDCPG p. 42).
Insulin-resistance signs such as acanthosis nigricans (SDCPG p. 20 risk-factor list).
Frailty, volume depletion or low blood pressure change SGLT-2 inhibitor safety (NG28 1.19.1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: HbA1c 5.7–6.4% or fasting glucose 100–125 mg/dL: lifestyle prevention, not diabetes treatment (SDCPG p. 20).
If response to medicines does not fit type 2 diabetes, revisit the diagnosis (NG28 1.22.3).
Review glucocorticoids, atypical antipsychotics and other diabetogenic drugs (SDCPG p. 20).

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: confirm the diagnosis, agree an individual HbA1c target, choose initial treatment (including the triggers for insulin) and start safely. Checked against SDCPG 2021 (pp. 20, 28, 31, 35, 42, 46–48) and NICE NG28 (updated 18 Feb 2026, sections 1.2, 1.5, 1.8 and 1.13–1.22).
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Figure 2 (glycaemic targets) in the Saudi guideline is an image and was not read; target ranges quoted come from its text on pp. 28 and 31.
Medicine doses were reused from the repository's earlier label-checked type 2 diabetes topic and were not re-opened on 14 Oct 2026.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not independently verified.
Haemoglobin variants are common in the region; the sources give the fructosamine and total glycated haemoglobin alternatives but no local prevalence.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Adult with suspected or new diabetes
ruleIn.expectedFinding: 6.5% or more diagnoses diabetes; repeat every 3–6 months until stable, then 6-monthly (NG28 1.5.1); SDCPG: at least twice a year when controlled, four times when not (p. 31).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Confirms diagnosis and sets the baseline for the target; if HbA1c is unreliable use fructosamine or total glycated haemoglobin.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Test at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and at least yearly. Stage CKD with eGFR and ACR together and act on the result (see the Diabetic Kidney Disease topic).

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Annual foot examination: sensation, pulses, skin and deformity

pathophysiology.summary: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure causes chronic hyperglycaemia; HbA1c reflects average glucose over about 3 months (SDCPG p. 28). Better control lowers complications: in UKPDS, microvascular events fell 25% and macrovascular events 15% (SDCPG p. 28). Pushing HbA1c below 7% raises hypoglycaemia and polypharmacy, so the target is individualised (SDCPG p. 28). Severe hyperglycaemia with catabolic features (weight loss, hypertriglyceridaemia, ketosis) reflects glucose toxicity and responds best to insulin (SDCPG p. 47). SGLT-2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular events, heart-failure admissions and kidney failure, so NICE pairs one with metformin from diagnosis (NG28 section 1.13 and its rationale).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm and classify
actions: Confirm with Table 2 criteria (SDCPG p. 20); repeat if asymptomatic.
Look for ketosis, weight loss and other catabolic features, and for diabetogenic drugs (SDCPG pp. 20, 47).
Record BMI at every visit (SDCPG p. 42).

clinicalManagement.title: Education and lifestyle
actions: Offer structured education at diagnosis with annual reinforcement; group education is the preferred option (NG28 1.2.1, 1.2.4; SDCPG p. 35).
Aim for more than 5% weight loss; dietary energy deficit of 500–750 kcal/day (SDCPG pp. 35, 42).

clinicalManagement.title: Agree an individual HbA1c target
actions: Most adults: below 7% (SDCPG p. 31). NICE: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) on lifestyle or non-hypoglycaemic drugs; 53 mmol/mol (7.0%) on a hypoglycaemia-associated drug (NG28 1.5.7).
Consider a relaxed target for older or frailer people, limited life expectancy, high hypoglycaemia risk or major comorbidity (NG28 1.5.9).
If HbA1c is below target without hypoglycaemia, keep it there (NG28 1.5.10).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose initial treatment by profile
actions: SDCPG: metformin first unless contraindicated; dual therapy if HbA1c is more than 1.5% above target (p. 46).
NICE: modified-release metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor; if metformin is not tolerated, SGLT-2 inhibitor alone (NG28 1.13.1–1.13.2).
Same as above: modified-release metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor (NG28 1.14.1, 1.17.1).
branches.condition: Heart failure or living with obesity

actions: Add subcutaneous semaglutide, up to 1 mg once weekly (NG28 1.15.1).
Metformin plus SGLT-2 inhibitor, and consider adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide (NG28 1.16.1).
eGFR 30 or more: metformin plus SGLT-2 inhibitor. eGFR 20 to under 30: dapagliflozin or empagliflozin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor. eGFR under 20: consider a DPP-4 inhibitor (NG28 1.18.1–1.18.3).
Modified-release metformin; add an SGLT-2 inhibitor only if frailty does not risk volume depletion or hypotension (NG28 1.19.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Introduce one drug at a time
actions: Introduce medicines stepwise, checking tolerability and effect of each (NG28 1.20.1).
Start metformin first; add the SGLT-2 inhibitor once metformin is at the maximum tolerated dose (NG28 1.20.2).
Before an SGLT-2 inhibitor, check DKA risk and fix modifiable risks, for example delay while on a ketogenic diet (NG28 1.21.1–1.21.2).
Tell people that a ketogenic or very-low-carbohydrate diet raises DKA risk on an SGLT-2 inhibitor (NG28 1.21.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Insulin or GLP-1 receptor agonist at presentation
actions: Criteria: HbA1c above 10%, glucose consistently above 300 mg/dL, severe weight loss or osmotic symptoms (SDCPG pp. 47–48).
Basal insulin 0.1–0.2 units/kg/day if HbA1c is below 8%; 0.2–0.3 units/kg/day if above 8%; titrate by 2 units every third day to the fasting target (SDCPG p. 48).
With symptoms of hyperglycaemia, consider insulin or a sulfonylurea and review once glucose is in target (NG28 1.8.1).
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Same day if criteria are met

clinicalManagement.title: Review and escalate
actions: HbA1c every 3–6 months until stable, then every 6 months (NG28 1.5.1).

If the target is not met about 3 months after starting, add a second drug (SDCPG p. 47). If HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol (7.5%) or more, reinforce lifestyle and adherence, aim for 53 mmol/mol (7.0%) and intensify (NG28 1.5.8).
Use the Treatment Intensification topic for the add-on choice.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Diabetes (any one, confirmed by repeat if asymptomatic)
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: HbA1c 6.5% or more; fasting glucose 126 mg/dL (7 mmol/L) or more; 2-h OGTT glucose 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or more; random glucose 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or more (SDCPG p. 20, Table 2)
HbA1c 5.7–6.4%; fasting glucose 100 to under 126 mg/dL; 2-h OGTT 140 to under 200 mg/dL (SDCPG p. 20, Table 2)

Most adults below 7%, within a 6.5–8% spectrum (SDCPG pp. 28, 31); NICE 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) on lifestyle or non-hypoglycaemic medicines, 53 mmol/mol (7.0%) on a hypoglycaemia-associated medicine (NG28 1.5.7)
HbA1c more than 1.5% above target (SDCPG p. 46); NICE offers metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor from diagnosis when there is no relevant comorbidity (NG28 1.13.1)
HbA1c above 10%, glucose consistently above 300 mg/dL, or catabolic features (SDCPG pp. 47–48)

nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review within 3 months, then HbA1c every 3–6 months until stable and every 6 months after (NG28 1.5.1); structured education reinforced each year.
mdtReferrals: Endocrinology if insulin is needed at presentation or the diagnosis is uncertain.
Ophthalmology, podiatry and renal services as complications are found (SDCPG p. 32 team list).
lifestyleAndDiet: Aim for more than 5% weight loss with an energy deficit of 500–750 kcal/day (SDCPG p. 42).
Ask about ketogenic or very-low-carbohydrate diets before an SGLT-2 inhibitor (NG28 1.21.3).
patientEducation: Explain that diabetes is lifelong and that treatment aims to prevent complications.
Offer a structured group education programme at diagnosis and each year (NG28 1.2.1, 1.2.4).
dischargeCriteria: Diagnosis confirmed, target agreed and documented.
Initial drugs started with tolerability checked and education booked.
